Thus, in the *Śrīrudrayāmala*, in the *Kedārakalpa*, within the dialogue between Śrīśvara and Kārttikeya, in the section on the method of practicing the Aghora mantra, this is the first chapter, titled "The Journey to Kailāsa with the Body" on the Great Path (*mahāpatha*) for the realization of the Supreme Brahman as one liberated while living (*jīvanmukta*), through the practice of the five Lords of Yoga (*pañcayogendra*). 1.
The Second Chapter. Śrīśvara said:

Oṃ. Of this Śrī Aghora mantra, Aghora is the seer (ṛṣi), Bṛhatī is the meter (chanda), Śrī Kālāgnirudra is the deity (devatā), Hrīṃ is the seed-syllable (bīja), Huṃ Phaṭ Svāhā is the power (śakti); its application (viniyoga) is in recitation for the sake of attaining the grace of Aghora.
Thus is the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*).
Now follows the ritual placement of the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa).
Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to both thumbs.
Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to the two index fingers.
Oṃ hrūṃ, homage to the two middle fingers.
Oṃ hraiṃ, homage to the two ring fingers.
Oṃ hrauṃ, salutation to the two little fingers.
Oṃ hraḥ, homage to both palms and backs of the hands.
Thus concludes the ritual placement of the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa).
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the heart and other limbs.
Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to the heart.
Oṃ hrīṃ, svāhā to the head.
Oṃ hrūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Oṃ hraiṃ hūṃ, for the armor.
Oṃ hrauṃ, vaṣaṭ to the three eyes.
Oṃ hraḥ, phaṭ to the weapon!
Thus ends the placement of the heart and other limbs (hṛdayādinyāsa).
Now, meditation.

Oṃ! [I bow to] the Lord who has Kailāsa as his seat, whose mass of matted hair blazes with the crescent moon, who is intent on gazing with his nose, who possesses three eyes, and who is seated in the heroic posture (vīrāsana).

I bow to the supreme Maheśa, who holds a seal and a coin, whose Gaurī shines upon his knee, whose face is serene, who has a serpent bound around his waist, and who observes the vows of a sage. || 1 ||
Thus ends the section on meditative concentration.
Now follows the mantra for recitation.
Oṃ kroṃ hruṃ phaṭ svāhā.
Now follows the dedication of the recitation (japasamarpaṇam).
Oṃ, accept this recitation performed by us, the secret more secret than the secret.
O God, O Maheśvara, may success be mine through your grace. || 2 ||
By this recitation, numbering thus many times, may the venerable Rudra in the form of Aghora be pleased.
Thus ends the offering of the recitation.
Then one should recite the hymn of praise.
Śrīśvara said:
Oṃ, salutation to Kāma, to Rudra; salutation to him who bears the form of liberation.
Salutations to you, whose self is the Nāda; salutations to you, whose self is the Bindu and the Kalās. || 3 ||
Salutation be to You who are in the form of the Liṅga; salutation to You who transcend the Liṅga.
You are the mother of all worlds; you alone are the father of the universe.
You are my brother, you are my well-wisher and friend, you are my beloved, and you are my grandfather.
Salutations to you, O Blessed Rudra, the Sun-god of immeasurable splendor. || 5 ||
Homage to Bhava, to Rudra, and to him who consists of the supreme waters.
Salutations always to Śarva, who is white in form and eternally fragrant. || 6 ||
And also to Paśupatī, whose splendor is like that of the purifying fire.
Salutations again and again to the exceedingly terrifying one, to the gentle one, and to the immortal one. || 7 ||
Obeisance to you, the fierce one, to the sacrificer, to the master of the yoga of action.
As for the worship that has been performed by me of the earthen lingas, [let that be mine]. || 8 ||
Therefore, may the Blessed Lord Rudra grant me my desired object.
Whoever recites this hymn according to the prescribed rule at the time of worship, || 9 ||
He shall become a universal monarch (cakravartin) and, in the end, go to the city of Śiva.

Thus ends the second chapter, titled "The Hymn to Sadāśiva-Aghora," in the *Mahāpatha-Śivadarśana* concerning the journey to Kailāsa with the physical body, for the attainment of the Supreme Brahman as a living-liberated one (*jīvanmukta*) through the practice of the five lords of yoga, within the *Kedārakalpa* of the *Śrī Rudrayāmala*, in the dialogue between Īśvara and Kārtikeya. || 2 ||
The Third Chapter. Śrīśvara said:

Oṃ. Of this Śrī Sadāśiva-kavaca, Bhṛgu is the seer (ṛṣi), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandas), Śrī Sadāśiva is the deity (devatā), and its application (viniyoga) is for the purpose of attaining Kailāsa during recitation.

Now, the armor-mantra (kavaca).

Therefore, with every effort, one who desires his own welfare [should act accordingly].
Having first understood the armor-mantra (kavaca), one should subsequently perform the recitation (japa).

Thus ends the third chapter, titled "The Armor of Aghora," in the *Śrīkedārakalpa*, within the *Rudrayāmala Tantra*, in the dialogue between Īśvara and Kārttikeya; concerning the attainment of the Supreme Brahman as one liberated while living through the practice of the five lords of yoga, on the Great Path, in the vision of Śiva, and regarding the journey to Kailāsa with the physical body. || 3 ||
